title: Citrate Buffer Preparation
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfyfjptn

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M citric acid solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 19.21 g of citric acid (MW 192.1 g·mol⁻¹) in deionized water and make up to 1 L to obtain a 0.1 M solution.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M sodium citrate solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 29.4 g of sodium citrate dihydrate (MW 294.0 g·mol⁻¹) in deionized water and make up to 1 L to obtain a 0.1 M solution. Do not use the pentahydrate form.

steps.title: Mix buffer to desired pH
steps.instruction: Combine the citric acid and sodium citrate solutions in the proportions required to reach a pH between 3.0 and 6.2, then add deionized water to bring the total volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Adjust final pH
steps.instruction: Measure the pH with a sensitive pH meter and adjust, if necessary, by adding small amounts of the acid or citrate solutions until the target pH is reached.

steps.title: Reagent caution
steps.instruction: Use sodium citrate dihydrate; the pentahydrate salt of sodium citrate is not recommended.
